solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Half-hearted complaint about priest in faith

indicators.note: the trimmed complaint goes around the priest, so it is placed about him
the word for a complaint has two letters at its heart; losing one of them leaves it only half-hearted

parts.note: a beef is a grumble or complaint
Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel

explanation.surface: A lukewarm grumble about a clergyman, set in matters of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-hearted' drops one of the two letters at the complaint's heart, and 'about' then wraps what is left round the priest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a creed or religious conviction held by a believer.

clue.text: A scan by supreme authority in Indian city

parts.note: an MRI is a medical scan (magnetic resonance imaging)
a tsar was the supreme ruler of Russia; the word also means anyone with supreme authority

explanation.surface: A medical scan ordered by a top official in a city of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Punjab city that is home to the Golden Temple of the Sikhs.

clue.text: Fool with right to split money which male's collected and solicit contributions

indicators.note: the fool and the right letter break into the money word, splitting it in two

parts.note: a pound is a unit of British money
an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the word for which has gathered the male inside it, so the male is collected

parts.note: that can stand for which, as in 'the book that I read'
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A clown and a right-wing type divide the cash a man has gathered, then go round asking for donations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to split' and 'collected' both signal one piece placed inside another; 'which' standing for 'that' is the easily missed step.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a cap is handed from person to person so that each can drop in money for a cause.

clue.text: Reckon place is within reach

indicators.note: the word for place sits within the word for reach

parts.note: to come to a place is to reach it
to put something is to place it

explanation.surface: A judgement that a location lies close enough to get to.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to calculate or work out a figure.

clue.text: Fish one recalled cooked in student accommodation

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters of these words have been prepared afresh, i.e. rearranged

explanation.surface: A fish that someone remembers being served in a college dining hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like an instruction but is just part of the letters that 'cooked' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a university building where undergraduates live during term.

clue.text: Entertainer misrepresenting his age

indicators.note: to misrepresent is to give a false version, so the letters are presented in a different order

explanation.surface: A performer lying about how old he is.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a Japanese hostess trained to entertain with music, dance and conversation.

clue.text: A bit of fruit lacking round division of farm?

indicators.note: lacking says the fruit part goes without the round letter

parts.note: the core is the central part of an apple or pear
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit missing its round shape, perhaps a part of a farm's produce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes the round letter. The question mark marks the definition as loose: a farm is not literally split into these units, but its land is measured in them.
explanation.definitionFit: Unit of land measure, so a farm's fields are counted in these portions.

clue.text: Label spell behind bars

definitions.meaning: a word or name given to something, as in a technical expression
the period of a prison sentence, as in serving time

explanation.surface: A tag naming a stint in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a name given to something, and the length of time a prisoner serves.

clue.text: Bother head of housing

indicators.note: the words head of are housing the answer, holding it inside them

explanation.surface: Trouble caused by the person in charge of housing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of housing' reads as a job title, but 'housing' is the signal that 'head of' contains the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: fuss, trouble or bother, as in much ado about nothing.

clue.text: A dope carelessly vacated recruitment outfit

parts.note: dope and gen are both slang for information

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving just its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A careless idiot walked out of the staffing company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' looks like a fool but means information.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a business that finds staff for employers is an employment bureau of this kind.

clue.text: Watches oversexed American in much of worthless society

indicators.note: the American soldier goes in the shortened word for worthless
much of a word is most of it, so its last letter goes

parts.note: vile can mean worthless or base
GI is a US soldier; British wartime jibe called GIs overpaid, oversexed and over here

explanation.surface: A randy American mixing in a contemptible social set.
explanation.walkthrough: The WWII gibe about American troops in Britain was that they were 'overpaid, oversexed and over here'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: night-long periods of keeping awake on guard or in prayer.

clue.text: Idle shop revamped in smart fashion

indicators.note: revamped means remodelled, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: An unused store has been refitted stylishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: refined, elegant and well-groomed.

clue.text: Maybe, bleak old tutor a few disrupted is one unsuited to situation

parts.note: the bleak is a small freshwater fish, and Maybe flags it as an example

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A gloomy old teacher, perhaps, is upset by a handful of people and feels out of place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bleak' looks like an adjective for the tutor, but it is the name of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone ill at ease in surroundings that do not suit them.

clue.text: Listless on reflection for long period

indicators.note: reflection in a mirror flips the order, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: listless means lacking energy, i.e. no E, with E the abbreviation for energy

explanation.surface: Thinking it over lazily for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'Listless' as NO E, having no energy (E), then turn it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an age or an immensely long stretch of time.

clue.text: Merit in militarist's tirade?

definitions.meaning: the question mark flags the punning split

explanation.surface: Something worth hearing in a warmonger's harangue.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to deserve or justify, and a punning tirade about combat.

clue.text: Mess in East End remains

indicators.note: Cockneys of the East End of London traditionally drop the h sound at the start of words

parts.note: a hash is a mess, as in making a hash of something

explanation.surface: A shambles left among the ruins in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is the traditional Cockney part of London, where speakers drop the H at the start of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the powdery residue left after burning is often called remains, as of a cremation.

clue.text: Relevant Australian writer according to friend's broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken out over the air, so the name is said aloud

parts.note: Germaine Greer, the Australian feminist writer, would be called by her first name by a friend

explanation.surface: A pertinent comment from an Australian author, as a friend reports on air.
explanation.walkthrough: Friends use first names, so the Australian writer Germaine Greer becomes just Germaine.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: pertinent or to the point in a discussion.

clue.text: Brand at an end in complete reorganisation

parts.note: a make is a brand of product
over means finished or at an end

explanation.surface: A company brand facing its finish undergoes a total overhaul.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a thorough transformation of appearance or structure.

clue.text: Beastly son taken with triumph of a sort

parts.note: a win is a triumph
the suffix -ish means somewhat or of a sort

explanation.surface: A lad delighted by a narrow victory turns nasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: piggish or nasty in behaviour, like a hog.

clue.text: Explosive musical beat, in short endlessly excellent thing

indicators.note: the three pieces go in the shortened word for short
without its last letter, so the end letter goes

parts.note: terse means short or curt
HE is the abbreviation for high explosive
Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
to whisk eggs is to beat them

explanation.surface: A dynamic musical number, in brief, is simply wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' trims the word for short, which then holds the other three pieces. 'in short' looks like 'briefly' but 'short' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something or someone outstandingly good, the bee's knees.

clue.text: Lower pointer in the main, we hear, for shoddy operator

parts.note: a lower is something that lows, or moos, such as a cow

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for a sea marker is to be said aloud

parts.note: a buoy is a floating marker pointing the way at sea, the main being the ocean

explanation.surface: Lower a signpost into the sea for a dodgy workman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' reads as 'drop down' but means 'one that lows'. 'the main' is an old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang: an unqualified tradesman who does slapdash work for cash.

clue.text: Storm engulfing a very tiny ruin

indicators.note: the word for storm swallows up the other letters, engulfing them

parts.note: to rage is to storm
V is the abbreviation for very, cut down tiny to one letter

explanation.surface: A tempest swallowing a minute wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to devastate or lay waste.

clue.text: Check on women excitedly consuming current Eastern dish

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: the rearranged women take in the current letter, consuming it
excitedly suggests agitation, so these letters are stirred up

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A restraint on women eagerly tucking into a meal of oriental food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excitedly' rearranges WOMEN as OWMEN, and 'consuming' takes I inside it before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Chinese-style plate of fried noodles.

clue.text: King, say, not working for period

indicators.note: on means working, so not working says the on letters are dropped

parts.note: a king is an honour card in bridge, like ace, queen and jack

explanation.surface: A monarch, perhaps, idle for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge and whist the top cards, ace to ten, are called honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: sixty minutes is a period of time.

clue.text: Change famous album missing jacket

indicators.note: a jacket is an outer cover, so the outside letters are lost

parts.note: Revolver is a celebrated 1966 Beatles album

explanation.surface: A well-known record sold without its sleeve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jacket' fits a record sleeve on the surface but here means the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to develop gradually or alter over time.

clue.text: Drink sealing success in dome

indicators.note: the drink seals the other piece inside it

parts.note: cola is a fizzy drink
up means ahead or winning, as in being one up

explanation.surface: A drink toasting a triumph under a domed roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small rounded roof on a building.

clue.text: Dry back (not half)

indicators.note: only half the word for back is used, its first three letters

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: Arid again, though not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' is British slang for 'very much', but here it means half the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine term: French for dry, used of champagne and other wines.

clue.text: Nervous, stressed gymnast keeps inside

indicators.note: the two words keep the answer inside them, across the gap

explanation.surface: An anxious, strained athlete keeps her feelings inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: tense, jumpy or on edge.
